questions.prompt: Which set shows the main components studied in Integrated Science?
questions.explanation: Integrated Science brings together ideas about living things, materials, energy, forces, and safe investigation.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the components of Integrated Science as a field of study.

questions.prompt: A Grade 7 learner observes bean seedlings growing near a classroom. Which component of Integrated Science is mainly involved?
questions.explanation: Biology studies living things, including plants, animals, and their life processes.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate components of Integrated Science to everyday examples.

questions.prompt: Integrated Science helps learners solve daily problems using evidence.
questions.explanation: Science uses observation, measurement, testing, and reasoning to explain and solve real problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of science in daily life.

questions.prompt: Which activity best shows Physics in daily life?
options: Using a ramp to push a loaded wheelbarrow
Testing lemon juice with litmus paper
questions.correctAnswer: Using a ramp to push a loaded wheelbarrow
questions.explanation: Physics includes forces, motion, energy, electricity, magnetism, and simple machines.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of science components in everyday activities.

questions.prompt: Why is it useful to learn Integrated Science in junior school?
options: It helps learners understand health, materials, energy, and the environment
It replaces all other learning areas
It is only for learners who want to be doctors
It teaches learners to guess without evidence
questions.correctAnswer: It helps learners understand health, materials, energy, and the environment
questions.explanation: Integrated Science supports safe decisions at home, school, farms, workshops, and the wider environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of science in daily life.

questions.prompt: Name one component of Integrated Science.
questions.explanation: Biology, Chemistry, and Physics are major components of Integrated Science.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the components of Integrated Science as a field of study.

questions.prompt: A learner says science is useful only inside a laboratory. Which response is best?
options: Science is also used in cooking, health, farming, transport, and communication
Science is never used outside a laboratory
Science cannot help people make decisions
Science is only the naming of apparatus
questions.correctAnswer: Science is also used in cooking, health, farming, transport, and communication
questions.explanation: Scientific knowledge is applied in many day-to-day tasks beyond the laboratory.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply understanding of science to daily life situations.

questions.prompt: Which laboratory hazard symbol usually warns about a substance that can catch fire easily?
questions.explanation: A flammable warning shows that a substance can ignite easily and should be kept away from flames.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common hazards and their symbols in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: Which action is safest when a chemical bottle has no label?
options: Report it to the teacher and do not use it
Smell it closely to identify it
Mix it with another unknown liquid
questions.correctAnswer: Report it to the teacher and do not use it
questions.explanation: Unknown chemicals may be harmful, so learners should avoid contact and ask a responsible adult.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety measures when working in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: Running in the laboratory can cause accidents.
questions.explanation: Running can lead to slips, collisions, spills, cuts, and burns in a laboratory.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the causes of common accidents in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: A learner gets a small heat burn during a teacher-guided activity. What First Aid should be done first?
options: Cool the burn under clean running water
questions.correctAnswer: Cool the burn under clean running water
questions.explanation: Cooling a minor burn with clean running water reduces heat and tissue damage before further care.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe First Aid measures for common laboratory accidents.

questions.prompt: Which situation is a common cause of cuts in the laboratory?
options: Handling broken glass with bare hands
questions.correctAnswer: Handling broken glass with bare hands
questions.explanation: Broken glass has sharp edges and should be handled using safe tools and teacher guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the causes of common accidents in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: Which personal protective item best protects the eyes from splashes?
questions.explanation: Safety goggles cover the eyes and reduce injury from splashes or small particles.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify safety equipment used in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: A class notices a liquid spill near an electrical socket. What should they do?
options: Move away and inform the teacher immediately
Step through the spill to test it
Switch the socket on and off
questions.correctAnswer: Move away and inform the teacher immediately
questions.explanation: A spill near electricity can cause shock, so learners should avoid it and report at once.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety measures in laboratory hazard situations.

questions.prompt: Which plan best prevents accidents before an investigation begins?
options: Read instructions, identify hazards, wear protection, and arrange materials safely
Start quickly before knowing the materials
Keep all bags on the workbench
Use any chemical if it looks clear
questions.correctAnswer: Read instructions, identify hazards, wear protection, and arrange materials safely
questions.explanation: Planning reduces risk because learners know the procedure, hazards, and protective actions.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan safe laboratory work and access to a healthy working environment.

questions.prompt: Name one common laboratory accident that First Aid can help manage.
questions.explanation: First Aid can help manage burns, cuts, chemical splashes, fainting, and minor bruises before medical help is given.
questions.learningOutcome: Name common accidents that may occur in a laboratory.

questions.prompt: Write a short safety plan for a group heating water in a beaker during a laboratory activity.
questions.correctAnswer: A good plan includes reading instructions, wearing goggles, using a heatproof mat, pointing the beaker away from people, using tongs if needed, and reporting accidents immediately.
questions.explanation: Heating activities need planning because hot glass, steam, flames, and spills can injure learners.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop safe procedures for laboratory activities.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is most suitable for measuring temperature in a science activity?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature, commonly in degrees Celsius.
questions.learningOutcome: Use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: Which apparatus is best for measuring a fixed volume of water more accurately than a beaker?
questions.explanation: A measuring cylinder has graduations for measuring liquid volume more accurately than an ordinary beaker.
questions.learningOutcome: Select appropriate apparatus for basic science tasks.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit for length?
questions.explanation: The metre is the SI base unit used to measure length.
questions.learningOutcome: Use SI units for basic quantities in science.

questions.prompt: Which quantity is measured in kilograms?
questions.explanation: Kilogram is the SI base unit for mass.
questions.learningOutcome: Use SI units for basic quantities in science.

questions.prompt: A learner reads a measuring cylinder while looking down from above. What error may occur?
questions.explanation: Parallax error occurs when a scale is read from an angle instead of at eye level.
questions.learningOutcome: Use apparatus correctly to obtain reliable measurements.

questions.prompt: Laboratory apparatus should be cleaned and stored safely after use.
questions.explanation: Cleaning and safe storage protect users and keep apparatus ready for later investigations.
questions.learningOutcome: Use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly matches an instrument to what it measures?
questions.explanation: A stopwatch measures time intervals, usually in seconds or minutes.
questions.learningOutcome: Match common science instruments with their uses.

questions.prompt: A group needs to measure the mass of soil samples before an experiment. Which apparatus should they choose?
questions.explanation: A balance is used to measure mass, so it suits comparison of soil sample masses.
questions.learningOutcome: Select and use appropriate instruments for measurements.

questions.prompt: Which practice best protects a thermometer from damage?
options: Hold it carefully and store it in its case after use
Use it to stir stones in a beaker
Leave it at the edge of a bench
Heat it directly in a flame without guidance
questions.correctAnswer: Hold it carefully and store it in its case after use
questions.explanation: Thermometers can break easily, so careful handling and safe storage protect both learners and equipment.
questions.learningOutcome: Use and care for apparatus and instruments safely.

questions.prompt: Which method can separate salt from a salt solution?
questions.explanation: Evaporation removes water as vapour and leaves dissolved salt behind.
questions.learningOutcome: Separate homogeneous mixtures using appropriate methods.

questions.prompt: Which example is a homogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform appearance throughout, like sugar solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify homogeneous mixtures in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: A mixture can contain substances that are not chemically combined.
questions.explanation: In a mixture, substances keep many of their properties and can often be separated physically.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the nature of mixtures.

questions.prompt: Which method is most suitable for separating different colours in ink?
questions.explanation: Chromatography separates soluble substances such as dyes as they move through paper at different speeds.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose appropriate methods for separating homogeneous mixtures.

questions.prompt: Why is distillation useful for obtaining clean water from salty water?
options: Water evaporates and condenses while salt remains behind
The salt changes into a plant
questions.correctAnswer: Water evaporates and condenses while salt remains behind
questions.explanation: Distillation uses evaporation and condensation to collect the liquid component from a solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline applications of separating homogeneous mixtures in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to recover sugar crystals from a sugar solution. Which process should be used carefully?
questions.explanation: Removing some water from a solution can allow dissolved sugar to form crystals.
questions.learningOutcome: Separate homogeneous mixtures using appropriate methods.

questions.prompt: Which daily activity uses separation of a mixture?
options: Evaporating salty water to obtain salt
Bending a wire into a hook
questions.correctAnswer: Evaporating salty water to obtain salt
questions.explanation: Salt production from salty water is an application of separating a solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline applications of separating mixtures in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Name one method used to separate a homogeneous mixture.
questions.explanation: Evaporation, distillation, crystallization, and chromatography can separate some homogeneous mixtures.
questions.learningOutcome: Name methods of separating homogeneous mixtures.

questions.prompt: Which fair test would best compare how temperature affects the rate of dissolving sugar?
options: Use equal sugar amounts and equal water volumes at different temperatures
Use different sugar amounts, cups, and stirring times
Taste every solution to check sweetness
Use only one cup and make no observations
questions.correctAnswer: Use equal sugar amounts and equal water volumes at different temperatures
questions.explanation: A fair test changes only the temperature while keeping other important conditions the same.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan an investigation related to mixtures using fair-test principles.

questions.prompt: Describe how a learner can safely obtain salt crystals from salty water in a school laboratory.
questions.correctAnswer: The learner should place salty water in an evaporating dish, heat gently under supervision, stop before splashing occurs, allow cooling, and observe salt crystals left behind.
questions.explanation: The method applies evaporation while controlling heat and avoiding burns or splashes.
questions.learningOutcome: Separate homogeneous mixtures safely using appropriate methods.

questions.prompt: What happens to blue litmus paper in an acidic solution?
questions.explanation: Acids change blue litmus paper to red.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify acids using litmus paper.

questions.prompt: What happens to red litmus paper in a basic solution?
questions.explanation: Bases change red litmus paper to blue.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify bases using litmus paper.

questions.prompt: Which item is commonly acidic?
questions.explanation: Lemon juice contains acid and has a sour taste, though chemicals should not be tasted in the laboratory.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common acids in daily life.

questions.prompt: Which material can be used to prepare a simple natural acid-base indicator?
questions.explanation: Some coloured plant extracts, such as hibiscus, can change colour in acids and bases.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare an acid-base indicator from plant extracts.

questions.prompt: Learners should taste unknown laboratory chemicals to know whether they are acidic or basic.
questions.explanation: Tasting unknown chemicals is unsafe; indicators should be used under teacher guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety when investigating acids and bases.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes many bases?
options: They feel slippery and can be corrosive
They are all safe to drink
They always turn blue litmus red
questions.correctAnswer: They feel slippery and can be corrosive
questions.explanation: Many bases feel slippery, but they must still be handled carefully because some are corrosive.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe physical properties of acids and bases.

questions.prompt: A solution turns blue litmus red and has no effect on red litmus. What is the solution most likely to be?
questions.explanation: An acidic solution changes blue litmus to red while red litmus remains red.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret litmus test results for acids and bases.

questions.prompt: Which use of a base is common in daily life?
questions.explanation: Bases are used in cleaning products such as soaps and some detergents.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline applications of acids and bases in real life.

questions.prompt: A learner tests vinegar with blue litmus and red litmus. Which observation should be recorded?
options: Blue litmus turns red, red litmus stays red
Red litmus turns blue, blue litmus stays blue
questions.correctAnswer: Blue litmus turns red, red litmus stays red
questions.explanation: Vinegar is acidic, so it changes blue litmus to red.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze results from litmus tests of household substances.

questions.prompt: Name one plant material that can be used to make a natural indicator.
questions.explanation: Coloured plant materials such as hibiscus petals or red cabbage leaves can act as natural indicators.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare an acid-base indicator from plant extracts.

questions.prompt: Which part of the male reproductive system produces sperm cells?
questions.explanation: The testes produce sperm cells and male sex hormones.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify parts of the male reproductive system.

questions.prompt: Which part of the female reproductive system produces ova?
questions.explanation: The ovaries produce ova and female sex hormones.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify parts of the female reproductive system.

questions.prompt: Which physical change commonly occurs in boys during adolescence?
questions.explanation: During adolescence, boys commonly experience voice deepening, growth of body hair, and body growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe physical changes that take place in boys during adolescence.

questions.prompt: Which physical change commonly occurs in girls during adolescence?
questions.explanation: Menstruation is one normal physical change that can begin during adolescence in girls.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe physical changes that take place in girls during adolescence.

questions.prompt: Adolescence can involve physical, emotional, and social changes.
questions.explanation: Adolescence affects body growth, emotions, relationships, and personal responsibilities.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe changes that take place during adolescence.

questions.prompt: Which organ receives and supports a developing baby during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: The uterus is a muscular organ where a baby can develop during pregnancy.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe functions of parts of the female reproductive system.

questions.prompt: Which habit helps manage body changes during adolescence?
options: Maintaining personal hygiene and asking trusted adults for guidance
Sharing personal towels all the time
questions.correctAnswer: Maintaining personal hygiene and asking trusted adults for guidance
questions.explanation: Cleanliness, reliable information, rest, and support from trusted adults help learners manage adolescence safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop a plan to manage developmental challenges during adolescence.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why adolescents may need emotional support?
options: Hormonal and social changes can affect moods and confidence
Emotions are never part of human life
questions.correctAnswer: Hormonal and social changes can affect moods and confidence
questions.explanation: Adolescence brings changes that can affect emotions, so support and healthy communication are important.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe social and emotional changes during adolescence.

questions.prompt: Which action shows respect when learning about reproductive health?
options: Using correct terms and avoiding jokes about classmates' bodies
Refusing to listen to health guidance
questions.correctAnswer: Using correct terms and avoiding jokes about classmates' bodies
questions.explanation: Respectful language protects dignity and helps everyone learn sensitive health topics safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Show responsible attitudes when learning about adolescence and reproductive health.

questions.prompt: A learner feels worried about rapid body changes. Which response is best?
options: Talk to a parent, guardian, teacher, nurse, or trusted counsellor
Use random medicine from a friend
questions.correctAnswer: Talk to a parent, guardian, teacher, nurse, or trusted counsellor
questions.explanation: Trusted adults and health workers can give accurate support and help manage concerns safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop a plan to manage developmental challenges during adolescence.

questions.prompt: Name one normal physical change that may occur during adolescence.
questions.explanation: Normal changes include body growth, body hair, voice changes in boys, breast development in girls, and menstruation in girls.
questions.learningOutcome: Name physical changes that take place during adolescence.

questions.prompt: Which comparison between sperm and ova is accurate?
options: Sperm are produced in testes, while ova are produced in ovaries
Sperm are produced in ovaries, while ova are produced in testes
Both are produced in the lungs
Both are produced in the stomach
questions.correctAnswer: Sperm are produced in testes, while ova are produced in ovaries
questions.explanation: Male and female reproductive cells are made in different reproductive organs.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare functions of parts of male and female reproductive systems.

questions.prompt: Which plan best supports a Grade 7 learner during adolescence?
options: Keep clean, eat balanced meals, sleep enough, exercise, and seek trusted guidance
Ignore hygiene and avoid all trusted adults
Use social media as the only health teacher
questions.correctAnswer: Keep clean, eat balanced meals, sleep enough, exercise, and seek trusted guidance
questions.explanation: A balanced plan supports physical health, emotional wellbeing, and responsible decision-making.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop a plan to manage developmental challenges during adolescence.

questions.prompt: Create a simple one-week self-care plan for managing adolescence changes at school and at home.
questions.correctAnswer: A strong plan includes daily bathing, clean clothes, balanced meals, enough sleep, exercise, respectful relationships, and a trusted adult to consult when worried.
questions.explanation: Planning helps learners manage body changes, emotions, hygiene, and support needs consistently.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop a plan to manage developmental challenges during adolescence.

questions.prompt: Which organ removes urea and excess water from blood to form urine?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter blood and form urine, helping remove wastes from the body.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify functions of parts of the urinary system in humans.

questions.prompt: Which part carries urine from each kidney to the urinary bladder?
questions.explanation: The ureters are tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify functions of parts of the urinary system in humans.

questions.prompt: Which part of the skin produces sweat?
questions.explanation: Sweat glands produce sweat, which helps remove some waste and cool the body.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify functions of parts of the human skin.

questions.prompt: The urinary bladder stores urine before it leaves the body.
questions.explanation: The bladder temporarily stores urine until urination occurs.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify functions of parts of the urinary system in humans.

questions.prompt: Which habit supports healthy kidneys?
options: Holding urine for very long periods every day
questions.explanation: Safe water helps the kidneys remove wastes and supports normal urine formation.
questions.learningOutcome: Maintain a healthy lifestyle to promote kidney health.

questions.prompt: Which action may increase the risk of kidney problems?
questions.explanation: Some medicines can harm the kidneys when taken wrongly or in unsafe amounts.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe causes of kidney disorders in human beings.

questions.prompt: Why is regular bathing important for skin health?
options: It removes sweat, dirt, and germs from the skin
It stops kidneys from filtering blood
questions.correctAnswer: It removes sweat, dirt, and germs from the skin
questions.explanation: Clean skin is less likely to develop bad odour, blocked pores, and some infections.
questions.learningOutcome: Promote skin health through daily hygiene activities.

questions.prompt: Which part of the skin detects touch, pain, heat, and cold?
questions.explanation: Nerve endings in the skin sense changes such as touch, pressure, pain, heat, and cold.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify functions of parts of the human skin.

questions.prompt: A learner keeps a daily log of water intake, exercise, bathing, and sleep. Which body systems does this mainly support?
questions.explanation: A daily health log can track habits that protect the skin and kidneys.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop and maintain a daily log of activities that promote skin and kidney health.

questions.prompt: Which symptom should prompt a learner to seek help from a trusted adult or health worker?
questions.explanation: Pain during urination may signal an infection or other health problem that needs proper care.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize signs that may require health support for the urinary system.

questions.prompt: Name one organ of the human urinary system.
questions.explanation: The urinary system includes kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra.
questions.learningOutcome: Name parts of the human urinary system.

questions.prompt: Which statement best compares the role of skin and kidneys in excretion?
options: Skin releases sweat, while kidneys remove wastes from blood to form urine
Skin pumps blood, while kidneys digest food
Skin makes ova, while kidneys make sperm
Skin stores urine, while kidneys make sound
questions.correctAnswer: Skin releases sweat, while kidneys remove wastes from blood to form urine
questions.explanation: Both skin and kidneys help remove wastes, but they do it in different ways.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare functions of the skin and urinary system in excretion.

questions.prompt: Which daily log entry is most useful for checking kidney-health habits?
options: Cups of safe water taken and times urine was passed
Colour of the classroom wall only
Number of songs heard on radio
questions.correctAnswer: Cups of safe water taken and times urine was passed
questions.explanation: Water intake and urination patterns can help a learner notice habits related to kidney and urinary health.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop and maintain a daily log of activities that promote kidney health.

questions.prompt: Create a simple daily log that a Grade 7 learner can use to promote skin and kidney health.
questions.correctAnswer: A useful log includes date, cups of safe water, bathing, clean clothes, physical activity, balanced meals, enough sleep, and any unusual skin or urination concerns reported to a trusted adult.
questions.explanation: A daily log turns healthy habits into observable evidence that can guide improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop and maintain a daily log of activities that promote skin and kidney health.

questions.prompt: Which item is a common source of electricity in a simple classroom circuit?
questions.explanation: A dry cell provides electrical energy that can drive current in a simple circuit.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sources of electricity in the environment.

questions.prompt: What is needed for an electric bulb to light in a simple circuit?
options: A plastic cup instead of a cell
questions.explanation: Electric current flows around a closed circuit; a gap stops the current.
questions.learningOutcome: Use electrical circuits to demonstrate flow of electric current.

questions.prompt: A switch can open or close an electric circuit.
questions.explanation: A switch controls a circuit by making or breaking the path for current.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the role of a switch in an electrical circuit.

questions.prompt: Which material is a good electrical conductor?
questions.explanation: Copper allows electric current to flow easily, so it is commonly used in wires.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify materials used in electrical circuits.

questions.prompt: Which appliance changes electrical energy mainly into heat energy?
questions.explanation: An electric iron uses electrical energy to produce heat for pressing clothes.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify electrical appliances used in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Which action is safest when using electricity at home or school?
options: Keep wet hands away from switches and sockets
Touch bare wires to see if they are live
Overload one socket with many appliances
questions.correctAnswer: Keep wet hands away from switches and sockets
questions.explanation: Water can increase the risk of electric shock, so electrical devices should be handled with dry hands.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety measures when using electricity in daily life.

questions.prompt: A bulb does not light in a simple circuit. Which is the most likely reason?
options: There is a break in the circuit
The cell and bulb are both suitable
questions.correctAnswer: There is a break in the circuit
questions.explanation: A break prevents current from flowing, so the bulb cannot light.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze simple circuit faults.

questions.prompt: Which arrangement correctly makes a simple circuit?
options: Cell, wire, switch, and bulb connected in a closed loop
Bulb placed beside a cell with no wire
Two plastic cups placed on a table
questions.correctAnswer: Cell, wire, switch, and bulb connected in a closed loop
questions.explanation: A simple working circuit needs a source, conducting path, load, and closed connection.
questions.learningOutcome: Construct simple electrical circuits to demonstrate current flow.

questions.prompt: Which source of electricity uses sunlight?
questions.explanation: Solar cells convert light energy from the Sun into electrical energy.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sources of electricity in the environment.

questions.prompt: Why are many electric wires covered with plastic insulation?
options: Plastic makes current flow outside the wire
questions.explanation: Plastic is an insulator, so it helps prevent current from passing into a person's body.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe use of materials in electrical circuits.

questions.prompt: Name one electrical appliance used at home or school.
questions.explanation: Examples include an electric iron, radio, television, phone charger, fan, fridge, and electric kettle.
questions.learningOutcome: Name electrical appliances used in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to test whether a material conducts electricity. Which method is best?
options: Place the material in a simple circuit and observe whether the bulb lights
questions.correctAnswer: Place the material in a simple circuit and observe whether the bulb lights
questions.explanation: A working test circuit can show whether a material allows current to pass through it.
questions.learningOutcome: Design simple activities to demonstrate flow of electric current.

questions.prompt: Plan a safe investigation to find out whether copper, plastic, and dry wood conduct electricity.
questions.correctAnswer: A good plan uses a dry cell, bulb, wires, and a switch, tests one material at a time in the gap, records whether the bulb lights, and avoids mains electricity.
questions.explanation: The plan tests conductivity fairly and safely using a low-voltage circuit.
questions.learningOutcome: Design safe simple circuits to test electrical conduction.

questions.prompt: Which material is attracted by a magnet?
questions.explanation: Iron is a magnetic material and is attracted by magnets.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify materials as magnetic or non-magnetic.

questions.prompt: What happens when like poles of two magnets are brought close together?
questions.explanation: Like magnetic poles repel each other, while unlike poles attract.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe properties of a magnet.

questions.prompt: A magnet has a north pole and a south pole.
questions.explanation: A magnet has two poles, commonly called north and south.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe properties of a magnet.

questions.prompt: Which pair contains only non-magnetic materials?
questions.explanation: Wood and plastic are not attracted by ordinary magnets.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify materials as magnetic or non-magnetic.

questions.prompt: Where is the magnetic force usually strongest on a bar magnet?
questions.explanation: Magnetic attraction is strongest near the north and south poles of a magnet.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe properties of a magnet.

questions.prompt: Which device uses a magnet to show direction?
questions.explanation: A compass has a magnetic needle that aligns roughly north-south.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline applications of magnets in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: A magnet picks up some pins from a mixture of pins and maize grains. Which separation idea is being used?
questions.explanation: A magnet can separate magnetic materials from non-magnetic materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply properties of magnets in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Which observation shows that unlike magnetic poles attract?
options: A north pole and south pole pull together
A plastic ruler bends in water
questions.correctAnswer: A north pole and south pole pull together
questions.explanation: Unlike poles are north and south; they attract when brought close.
questions.learningOutcome: Investigate properties of magnets.

questions.prompt: Which use of magnets is common in daily life?
questions.explanation: Small magnets can hold doors, bags, and some covers closed.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline applications of magnets in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Name one material that is attracted by a magnet.
questions.explanation: Iron, steel, nickel, and cobalt are common magnetic materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify magnetic materials.

questions.prompt: Which fair test best compares the strength of two bar magnets?
options: Count how many identical paper clips each magnet can hold under the same conditions
Use different objects for each magnet and guess
Paint one magnet and ignore the other
questions.correctAnswer: Count how many identical paper clips each magnet can hold under the same conditions
questions.explanation: Using the same type of clips and procedure makes the comparison fair.
questions.learningOutcome: Design simple investigations of magnet properties.

questions.prompt: A learner concludes that all metals are magnetic after testing only an iron nail. What is the weakness in this conclusion?
options: Only one metal was tested, so the evidence is not enough
The conclusion used too many metals
questions.correctAnswer: Only one metal was tested, so the evidence is not enough
questions.explanation: A fair conclusion needs enough evidence from several metals, because some metals are not attracted by magnets.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze evidence from investigations of magnetic and non-magnetic materials.

questions.prompt: Plan an investigation to classify iron nails, aluminium foil, plastic buttons, and steel paper clips as magnetic or non-magnetic.
questions.correctAnswer: A good plan uses one magnet, tests one object at a time, records attracted or not attracted in a table, repeats if needed, and classifies each material from the evidence.
questions.explanation: The investigation uses observable attraction to sort materials into magnetic and non-magnetic groups.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify magnetic and non-magnetic materials through investigation.
